title: Myklebust 1988 thoracic PLL failure force by level

quantity.name: failure force
quantity.definition: maximum tensile force before load decreases with increasing deflection (peak load), in situ isolated ligament, 10 mm/s

source.authors: Myklebust JB, Pintar F, Yoganandan N, Cusick JF, Maiman D, Myers TJ, Sances A Jr
source.sample: 402 ligaments (C2-S1 plus upper cervical) from 41 fresh male cadavers; 2-5 specimens per ligament and level (Table 1 footnote); SSL only from C7-S1. Same laboratory and mechanical data set later used by Pintar 1992 (lumbar ligaments, 38 cadavers)

protocol.summary: Ligamentous spine kept at 2 C, tested within 1-3 days of death, moist with Ringer's solution; divided at C5-6 or T2-3 and T10-11 or T9-10. In situ isolation: at each level the disc and all supporting structures except the ligament under study were sectioned; vertebral bodies above and below fixed with Steinmann pins in a frame; ligament pulled in direct axial tension at a constant rate of 1 cm/s (10 mm/s, NOT quasi-static) on an MTS electrohydraulic system; deflection from the LVDT, confirmed by a potentiometer across the two vertebrae. Failure = maximum point at which load continued to decrease with increasing deflection. No cross-sectional areas or initial lengths reported (no stress or strain). JC tested as a bilateral unit including the facet joints; ISL/SSL divided at the end of the spinous process.
how_to_simulate: Bone-ligament-bone unit of the named ligament at the stated level, all other structures removed (in situ isolation)
Pull along the ligament's line of action at 10 mm/s to failure (peak load)
Report peak force (N) and the deflection at peak force (mm)
